ca_needles_the.blurb: The Needles are a cluster of granite spires on a narrow ridge high above the Kern River in the southern Sierra, near the southern end of the Great Western Divide. The setting is remote, with steep walls rising straight from the ridge. Almost all of the climbing is trad, with a few top-rope, sport and boulder problems mixed in. Grades are mostly 5.10 and 5.11, with a solid group of 5.12s and a smaller number of moderates between 5.7 and 5.9. The Witch, The Sorcerer and The Warlock hold the most climbs, alongside Voodoo Dome.

ma_tompson_st_reservation.blurb: Tompson St. Reservation lies in Gloucester on Cape Ann, on the Massachusetts North Shore. The terrain is rugged, with a red maple swamp, a beaver pond and exposed granite outcrops scattered across it. The climbing is almost entirely bouldering, spread over a large, expansive area, with a handful of trad and top-rope routes on the crags. Boulder problems run from about V1 to V8, and most fall between V3 and V6, so it suits climbers working at a solid intermediate level or above. Mount Jacob Boulders holds the most climbs, followed by Concord St. Entrance and Essex Greenbelt Area. Little Elephant Head and Eagle Rock Crag hold the roped lines.

mi_copper_country.blurb: Copper Country covers climbing on the Keweenaw Peninsula, the long arm of Michigan's Upper Peninsula that reaches into Lake Superior. Most of it is north of Houghton along Cliff Drive. The cliffs are basalt, running from about 30 up to roughly 150 feet, with slab and face climbs plus easy to moderate cracks. Bouldering holds the most climbs, mostly V0 to V5, and trad comes next, mostly 5.7 to 5.9, with a few top-rope and sport lines. Winter adds ice at Cliff Drive, Hungarian Falls and Houghton-Douglass Falls, although the ice at Cliff Drive is seasonal and sparse. The two main sub-areas are Cliff Drive Bouldering and Cliff Drive Roped.

mo_swope_park_bouldering.blurb: Swope Park Bouldering is in Kansas City, Missouri, inside Swope Park between a golf course and Highway 71. The climbing is all bouldering on limestone, with rough blocks that give short, unusual features. Problems are mostly low, around 10 to 15 feet tall, and sit starts are the norm. Grades run from V0 to V8, with most problems between V0 and V4, so there is plenty for newer boulderers and a harder tail on top. Swope Boulders holds the most climbs, followed by Fox Hollow Trail and Fireman's Memorial Boulders, and smaller zones sit along Blue River Road and Oldham Road.
